tool.name: minibwa index builder
tool.command: #set $fasta_file_name = str($all_fasta_source.fields.path).split('/')[-1] mkdir -p '${out_file.extra_files_path}' && ln -s '${all_fasta_source.fields.path}' '${out_file.extra_files_path}/${fasta_file_name}' && minibwa index -s '$s' -u '$u' ## -t is only effective without -l, -b is only effective with it #if str($l) == "-l": -l #if str($b): -b '$b' #end if #else: -t "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" #end if $meth '${out_file.extra_files_path}/${fasta_file_name}' && rm '${out_file.extra_files_path}/${fasta_file_name}' && cp '$dmjson' '$out_file'

param.label: Build the additional BS-seq index
param.help: Adds the FM-index needed to map directional bisulfite sequencing reads with the --meth option of the minibwa mapper. It is written next to the regular index, which stays usable for ordinary mapping, but it takes extra build time and disk space.

param.label: Suffix array sample rate, as 1/(2^INT)
param.help: -u; default=4; a larger value yields a smaller index at the cost of slower mapping

param.label: Use the low-memory BWT construction algorithm
param.help: -l; a GPL'd algorithm that needs less memory for large genomes. It is single threaded, so the thread count has no effect when it is enabled.

param.label: Block size for the low-memory algorithm
param.help: -b; default=10m; only effective together with the low-memory algorithm above. Accepts suffixes, e.g. 10m.

tool.help:
.. class:: infomark
**Notice:** If you leave name, description, or id blank, it will be generated automatically.
minibwa is a successor to BWA-MEM that aligns short reads and accurate long reads to a reference genome. It combines the variable-length seeding of BWA-MEM with the chaining and base-level alignment of minimap2, and additionally supports Hi-C reads and directional bisulfite sequencing reads.
This data manager builds a minibwa reference index (a ``.mbw`` and a ``.l2b`` file) with ``minibwa index`` and adds it to the ``minibwa_indexes`` tool data table, so that it can be selected as a built-in index in the minibwa mapper.
All options of ``minibwa index`` are available: the random seed for ambiguous bases (``-s``), the suffix array sample rate (``-u``, a larger value gives a smaller index but slower mapping), and the low-memory BWT construction algorithm (``-l``) with its block size (``-b``). The low-memory algorithm is single threaded and is worth enabling when a large genome does not index within the memory available to the data manager job; otherwise the index is built with all allocated cores.
Ticking **Build the additional BS-seq index** also creates a ``.meth.mbw`` file. That file is required by the mapper's *Directional bisulfite sequencing reads* library type; without it such a job fails to load the index. The regular index is built either way, so an index built with this option covers both ordinary and bisulfite mapping.
